q: A Lyapunov function V for ẋ = f(x) near an equilibrium x* satisfies:
opts: V(x*)=0, V(x)>0 for x≠x*, and V̇(x) = ∇V·f(x) ≤ 0 along trajectories
V is a constant of motion (V̇=0)
exp: A Lyapunov function is positive definite near x* and non-increasing along trajectories. It proves stability without solving the ODE. If V̇<0 (strict), it proves asymptotic stability — LaSalle gives a sharper criterion.
